Whiteboard popup review (2026-09-06, Claude Fable): committed locally, not deployed. Write-up in docs/whiteboard_review_2026-09-06.md. App-side bridge in AlloFlowANTI.txt read, NOT changed (origin-checked to the CDN, which is the app's own origin; fine). SECURITY (popup-only fix): the popup trusted whoever opened it. The app opens it by NAME ('alloflow-whiteboard'); a page already open in the same browser can pre-create a window of that name, the app's window.open then navigates it here and that page stays window.opener, and Save to AlloFlow posted the drawing to it with target '*'. Now Save and AI wait for an ack from a trusted origin (alloflow-cdn.pages.dev + *.alloflow-cdn.pages.dev over https, localhost, and the opaque 'null' the desktop bundle reports) and drawing-bearing posts go only to the pinned origin; hello/closed may still go to '*'. 'null' is accepted but never used as targetOrigin (that was July's muteness bug; whiteboard_recording.test.js updated to pin the property in its new shape). A stronger fix (one-time token in the URL, echoed in the ack) needs two lines in ANTI's openWhiteboard; left for a quiet moment on that file. Also: AI buttons used the disabled attribute while busy (focus dropped for the whole generation) -> aria-disabled + click guard, Record keeps disabled only when MediaRecorder is absent; choosing a template REPLACED the whole drawing with no confirmation -> appended below the lowest existing element via offsetSkeletonBelow, select resets; empty export used alert() -> inline flash; toolbar 12px/30px -> 13px/44px. Verified: tests/whiteboard_bridge_review.test.js (11, allowlist + template offset lifted from the page) + whiteboard_recording (7) + gif_encoder (9); Chromium smoke standalone with the real Excalidraw 0.17.6 from jsdelivr: mounted, AI bar hidden, Save disabled, no dialog on empty export, second template lands BELOW the first, select resets, PNG downloads, 44px/13px toolbar, zero page errors. NOT done: theme propagation (needs ?theme= from ANTI's openWhiteboard), i18n (popup is English, no lang param), SRI on the jsdelivr bundles. Process: compare-and-swap writer, mirror byte-identical, inline script syntax-checked, pathspec commit with only the new test + doc added. No deployment or push.

Timeline Studio review (2026-09-06, Claude Fable): committed locally, not deployed. Full write-up in docs/timeline_studio_review_2026-09-06.md. SECURITY: the companion window (timeline_studio/timeline_studio.html) accepted allotimeline-data from ANY window and TimelineJS renders text fields as HTML, so any page that opened the companion URL could inject markup on the CDN origin. Now requires opener AND an exact origin allowlist (own origin, alloflow-cdn.pages.dev and *.alloflow-cdn.pages.dev over https, localhost). A first draft reused the module's loose alloflow host pattern and the retired *.web.app suffix; the test caught alloflow.evil.example passing. Do not reuse companionUrl's isAlloHosted regex as a security boundary anywhere. Studio side ignores messages from windows it did not open and posts to COMPANION_ORIGIN, not '*'. Also: paste mode sent model output unescaped and the title was raw in both modes (both escaped now); the companion always opened DARK because nothing passed ?theme= and the host has no alloflow-theme-change broadcast (studio now passes hostTheme()); gradeLevel prop was ignored (now seeds the select via gradeToLevel); the manual-builder drawer was focusable while closed, its toggle had no aria-expanded, and once open it COVERED the header toggle so a mouse user could not close it (Playwright: drawer intercepts pointer events); now inert+hidden when closed, close button + Escape inside, focus returned. Verified: tests/timeline_studio_review.test.js (16) + the six existing timeline suites (52); Chromium smoke standalone confirmed every behaviour incl. toggleCoveredWhileOpen=true before the close button. DEFERRED, needs a quiet moment on ui_strings.js: all 61 timeline_studio.* keys are absent, so the whole modal is English in every language. Harvest by matching tr(t, 'timeline_studio.X', 'fallback') across timeline_studio_module.js (this session's script: C:/tmp/harvest_ts.cjs), then register_ui_strings with the snapshot/restore guard. The other session had ui_strings MM at the time. Process: compare-and-swap writer for all four files, mirrors byte-identical, pathspec commit with only the two new files added. No deployment or push.

Brain Atlas pathway playback narrated twice (2026-09-06, Claude Fable): committed locally, not deployed, BUT LANDED IN THE WRONG COMMIT. Look for it in d070e95ca 'Virtual Dissection Lab: the probe stops asking for what the student just did', not under a Brain Atlas message. What happened: another session had five dissection files pre-staged in the shared index; my git add joined them; that session's git commit fired between my add and my commit and swept my five files under its message; my commit then found nothing staged. No content was lost or altered on either side, only the attribution. History was not rewritten, since others may already build on it. RULE FROM THIS: on this tree never git add then git commit. Use git commit -m msg -- <paths> with no prior add; it commits exactly those paths from the working tree, ignores whatever anyone else has staged, and leaves their staged entries for them. And if git diff --cached ever shows files you did not touch, stop; someone is mid-commit. Every auto-advance during guided pathway playback already announces 'Step N, label. description' via announceToSR, and prev/next do the same. The progress counter beside the transport was also aria-live, so each step produced a second bare 'N / total' announcement every 0.9 to 2.6 s for the whole playback: the live-region-narrates-the-animation pattern. The counter stays visible and stops being live. It was the only timer-driven live region in the tool; the rest change on user actions. PROCESS CHANGE, per Aaron's instruction today that no one's work gets clobbered: the port went through a compare-and-swap writer (C:/tmp/safe_edit.cjs) that re-reads immediately before writing and refuses to write a stale buffer, and before staging the working-tree bytes were diffed against what the writer produced. This round's diff to the tool is exactly one line. ui_strings.js was left untouched because another session has it modified in the working tree; a snapshot-and-restore guard (C:/tmp/ui_strings_guard.cjs) is ready for the next round that needs keys. Validation: tests/brain_atlas_pathway_narration.test.js (4 tests) plus all 32 Brain Atlas files, 407 tests, in three groups at --maxWorkers=1. No golden movement. No deployment or push.

Brain Atlas answer surfaces keep focus (2026-09-06, Claude Opus): committed locally, not deployed. Same defect as the June fix, in the places that matter most. A disabled button leaves the tab order, so answering removed the element under focus and left the new feedback reachable only by tabbing from the top again. The authored-card checks have used aria-disabled since June; the Brain Quiz, Function Match, the Find It in 3D challenge and the Stimulation Lab patient radio group had not. That was every remaining graded choice in the tool. The radio group was worse: a disabled radio is skipped by the arrow-key handling a radio group depends on, so answering broke the navigation model too. Two of the four had no guard behind the disabled attribute, which made them more than a focus bug: in the Brain Quiz a second click overwrote quizFeedback AND incremented quizScore and quizCorrect again; in the radio group it overwrote the guess. Both now return before touching state, and a test pins that the guard sits before the write. Function Match needed only the attribute, since pickFm already refused a second answer. Left alone deliberately: controls that are genuinely unavailable (zoom at its limit, empty study set) stay disabled. Validation: tests/brain_atlas_answer_focus.test.js (8 tests) plus all 31 Brain Atlas files, 403 tests, in three groups at --maxWorkers=1. The quiz golden moved (the option markup gained aria-disabled) and was re-baselined with the filter before -u. No new ui_strings keys. PORT NOTE: my idempotency marker for this port was 'if (fmAns) return;', which already existed inside pickFm, so the first run reported 'already ported' and changed nothing. Pick a marker that only your own edit can produce. SWEEP NOTE: this commit also carries another session's in-flight work in the same file, a module-scope __alloT helper and about thirty screen-reader announcements wrapped through it. It looked coherent and complete rather than half-written, and all 31 suites pass with it in, but it is theirs, not mine, and its stem.brainatlas.sr_* keys are not registered in ui_strings by this commit. No deployment or push.

Brain Atlas quiz answer-position bias fixed (2026-09-06, Claude Opus): committed locally, not deployed. The Brain Quiz ordered its four options with sort(function(){return Math.random()-0.5;}), which is not a shuffle. Measured in this engine on a four-item array: the answer landed in the first or last slot 31.2% of the time and in each middle slot 18.7%, so guessing an end option was worth about a third more than guessing at random. The same comparator picked the distractors, so some regions were systematically over-offered as wrong answers; for a three-item list the skew was 49.9% against 12.5%. All three uses now go through one brainAtlasShuffle helper that prefers window.fisherYatesShuffle when the shell has published it and otherwise runs an identical local Fisher-Yates. This is the same answer-position class already swept in other tools in this repo. PORT NOTE: this file spells the same character both ways on neighbouring lines, real UTF-8 on one and a backslash-u escape on the next, so every anchor has to be written the way its own line spells it. Brain Atlas sentences carry their values as placeholders (2026-09-06, Claude Opus): committed locally, not deployed. Wrapping whole labels still left the sentences that carry a value inside them, built by string joining: "Reveal " + name + " on the " + side + " side". A translator never sees a sentence there, and no language with different word order can be produced from it. Most are aria-labels, so the worst-affected learners are screen-reader users outside English. THE BLOCKER, worth knowing for every STEM tool: the shell's t takes either a string fallback or a params object, never both, and a string fallback turns interpolation off (stem_lab_module.js ~7678 sets _params only when the second argument is an object; AlloFlowANTI.txt ~5959 does the substitution). Every string in this tool relies on its fallback, so parameterised strings were impossible through that path. The tool's own t wrapper now takes (key, fallback, params) and substitutes after deciding whether the text came from the pack or the fallback, so both paths get filled. It also replaces every occurrence of a name; the shell's version uses String.replace with a string pattern and so fills only the first. Existing two-argument calls are unchanged. 24 sentences rewritten with named placeholders: keyboard-shortcut summary, search-result side pickers, study set actions and counts, round summary, cutaway readouts and orientation map, gestational week readout, compare tray count, recenter and pronounce actions, reading-level buttons, AI explanation button. Nine lines still concatenate; each chooses between several messages in a nested conditional and needs its branches separated first, which is a code-shape change rather than a wording one. No golden movement. 25 ui_strings keys registered and mirrored; clobber check run, nothing to restore. No deployment or push.

Brain Atlas myth-card copy (2026-09-05, Claude Opus): committed locally, not deployed. Each Neuromyths card can be copied as plain text (verdict and its meaning, claim, evidence, alternative, source and link) for handing to a teacher or family in an email or report. The copied text ends with a line saying the findings are group level and that it is not a diagnosis or medical advice, so the limits travel with the words. Routed through window.alloCopyText rather than the Clipboard API: Canvas refuses navigator.clipboard by permissions policy, so a direct call fails for every Canvas user while passing jsdom and Playwright. Standalone fallback uses a hidden textarea plus execCommand, and since that needs the click transient activation the text is built synchronously; tests/brain_atlas_myth_copy.test.js asserts no navigator.clipboard anywhere in the file and no await or fetch between the click and the copy (comments stripped before that assertion, since the comment explaining the rule contains the word). The result line is scoped to its own card. Five ui_strings keys. Also raised the timeout on one pre-existing test, the refinements all-canvases contract, from vitest 5s default to 30s: it renders every view, so its cost grew when the Neuromyths view made 23, and it measured about 7.6s alone on this machine. Assertions unchanged. Worth knowing for anyone reading red runs here: a full 23-file parallel run reported 2, then 8, then 2 different failures on three consecutive runs while every file passed alone, so treat a broad failure as contention until a single-file run reproduces it, and check for "Test timed out in 5000ms" rather than an assertion message. No deployment or push.

Brain Atlas chemical-imbalance card (2026-09-05, Claude Opus): committed locally, not deployed. Added a ninth Neuromyths card for the claim that depression is caused by a chemical imbalance, the misconception most likely to arise in a medication conversation with a family. The tool already hedged this theory in two places citing Moncrieff, so the card makes an existing position explicit rather than taking a new one. Verdict is oversimplified, not debunked: depression involves real biology, it is the specific low-serotonin story that is unsupported. The card states that the 2022 umbrella review was itself contested, that whether a medicine helps is a separate question from whether the imbalance story explains why, that antidepressants help some people with modest average benefit and more in severe depression, that the phrase spread through 1990s advertising, and that a fixed-defect framing has been associated with more pessimism about recovery. The alternative says medication decisions belong with the prescriber and never with a lesson or an app. Links to the serotonin region. Chips regridded to three rows of three; only the three claims with a published survey figure carry a belief bar and no number was invented for the rest. Canvas re-rendered and inspected at 760 and 360 px. One ui_strings key. FOR AARON: the serotonin region own if-damaged text still reads "serotonin depletion contributes to depression", closer to the deficiency framing than the hedge in its own function field; flagged in docs/brain_atlas_plain_language_notes.md rather than changed, since it is a clinical wording call. Every claim on this card needs the same red pen as the ADHD and autism cards. No deployment or push.

Built the view Aaron requested in docs/brain_atlas_review.md section 7 as a new Evidence group with eight cards: learning styles (debunked), left/right-brained people (oversimplified), the ten-percent myth (debunked), the age-three window (oversimplified), brain-training apps (oversimplified), ADHD brain differences and the autistic brain (real but small, not diagnostic; ENIGMA consortia), and the retinal-photo ADHD model (promising, not proven; Choi et al. 2025, matched case-control caveat). Each card has claim, evidence, alternative, verdict badge, and a source link; the view panel states that nothing is a diagnosis or treatment claim. Canvas shows Dekker et al. 2012 UK teacher endorsement bars for three claims plus verdict chips that open cards; pixel-rendered at 760px and 360px and inspected, caption moved above the chips after a phone overlap. Myth cards carry no damage field so they never enter the localization quiz. Registered 33 stem.brainatlas keys in ui_strings.js and the desktop copy; sources recorded in docs/brain_atlas_plain_language_notes.md. Validation: 19 Brain Atlas suites, 255 tests; golden re-baselined for 23 views (every digest moved by exactly one button, the Evidence tab); new tests/brain_atlas_neuromyths.test.js locks the framing. Source/desktop mirror parity and node --check passed. The commit was built from HEAD plus only this work, so the other session's uncommitted six-line contrast patch and the unrelated uncommitted ui_strings additions stay in the working tree untouched. INCIDENT: one vitest call put -u before the file filter and rewrote 44 snapshots suite-wide; the four files that run touched (dino_lab, stem_big_tools, stem_longtail_tools, stem_sim_tools) were reverted to HEAD by mtime evidence; stem_tool_golden's snapshot was already modified by another session before the run and was left alone. Every ADHD and autism sentence is for Aaron to red-pen before deploy. No deployment or push.

Five fixes: (1) **CSRF/DNS-rebinding guard** on the private 127.0.0.1 API (`handleApi`) — rejects non-loopback `Host` and cross-origin state-changing requests; the loopback API previously had no Origin/Host validation, so any web page could drive `/api/config`, `/api/engine/start`, etc. on a guessable port. (3) **HTTPS enforced** for engine/ASR binary+model downloads + **optional SHA-256 pin** (`localEngine`/`localAsr` `.binarySha256`/`.modelSha256`) verified before install (the binaries are spawned). (4) `shell.openExternal` restricted to `http`/`https`/`mailto`. (5) `extraArgs` sanitized before spawn. Validation: `node --check` both files; `runtime:smoke` PASS with new asserts (CSRF 403, rebinding 403, `__proto__` PATCH → no pollution, same-origin POST still 200); `electron:check` PASS. ### 2026-09-10 — Zoom Gallery + Scale Explorer are LIVE; the CDN smoke test was a vacuous guard (Claude Code) @711ead205
- **Both tools deployed** by another session's full deploy (`Post-deploy: update CDN hash refs to @0897e3e98`). CDN byte sizes match local exactly (63,217 / 85,586). The pop-out `zoom_gallery/zoom_gallery.html` answers 308 → extensionless URL — that is Cloudflare clean-URL normalisation, the query string survives, and the served body is the real file (76,506 B). Not a bug.
- ★★★**`tests/e2e/13-stem-tools-all-cdn.spec.ts` — the post-deploy guard for tool modules — could not fail.** Two defects:
  1. It hand-listed **104** ids while the app loads **147**. 44 tools had no CDN check at all: gisstudio, arccity, spacestation, treelab, machinelab, geologyexplorer, nuclearlab, heatlab, alphafold, cellatlas, particlelab3d, the three shelves, both of mine, and more. Now READS `stemToolModules` from `AlloFlowANTI.txt` — the exact set the app requests — so a wired tool is covered automatically. (A **fifth wiring point**, now self-maintaining.)
  2. Its "looks like JS" regex (`/window\.StemLab|registerTool|React|createElement|module/i`) **matched the SPA fallback page**: Cloudflare serves a missing path as the app shell — 200, text/html, ~380 KB — and that shell contains "React". Proof: the listed `algebraCAS` (miscased; real file is `algebracas`) had been PASSING on the fallback, and so does `stem_tool_definitely_not_real.js`. Now asserts `content-type ~ /javascript/`, rejects a body starting with `<`, and requires the registration call. Plus a sanity test that the list parsed non-empty, so it cannot go green by checking nothing.
- Live result: **148 passed** — all 147 loaded tools are genuinely served as JavaScript today.
- Generalisable: any "is the file live" check on this CDN MUST assert content-type. `resp.ok()` + "body > N bytes" + a loose regex is exactly the shape that passes a 404-as-HTML. Same class as the "5 scripts 404-as-HTML" finding in the role-modes review.

## 2026-09-10 (late) — Scale Explorer / Zoom Gallery: the real host, not a harness

Every earlier check of the two new tools used a harness or a mock. Opening them in the REAL deployed app through the shell deep link (`/app/?tool=scaleExplorer`, `?tool=zoomGallery`) found two separate defects, one of them lab-wide. Both are fixed locally and verified in the real host (`react-scripts start` on :3000, which runs App.jsx with the public/ assets); the live CDN still shows the old behaviour until the next deploy.

**1. `?tool=scaleExplorer` opened the plain app with no error.** `_alloReadShellDeepLinkTool` validates against `_ALLO_STEM_DEEP_LINK_MAP`, generated from `tool_index.json`, last rebuilt 09-03. A new STEM tool therefore has SIX wiring points: catalog tile, `_pluginOnlyTools`, ANTI loader list, `build.js`, the CDN smoke spec, and `tool_index.json` (→ map + `/_redirects`). `fieldJourneys` had the same gap; `fractionViz` had never been indexed at all (builder matched only inline `registerTool('id', {`). Fixed @4b4a176f7: index rebuilt to 150, builder accepts a named config, reachability gate gained a fifth check that reads the exemptions from source. `tests/tool_index.test.js` was red at HEAD for this; it is green now, but note it goes red the moment ANY session changes a tool's desc/label without rerunning `node dev-tools/build_tool_index.cjs` (saw one transient during this pass while arccity/geologyexplorer were being edited).

**2. `?tool=zoomGallery` showed "Zoom Gallery could not load — The plugin loaded but did not register with STEAM Lab."** Root cause is in the host and affects every shared link on a cold load: the deep link requests the plugin `<script>` the moment the app is ready, while `stem_lab_module.js` (~560 KB) is still queued in the deferred module pump, so the plugin executes before `window.StemLab` exists. Measured the two orders offline in Chromium (`order_check*.cjs` in my scratchpad):
- 21 plugins `return` when StemLab is absent → never register → the error card. Verified LOST for all 21: alphafold, archstudio, cellatlas, circuitshelf, citylab, coasterlab, cyberdefense, datalab, geologyexplorer, geometryworld, heatlab, moleculeshelf, nuclearlab, particlelab3d, printlab, simshelf, spacestation, timeline, weathersystems, zoomgallery, scaleexplorer. So `/geology-explorer`, `/space-station`, `/geometry-world`, `/arch-studio` etc. are broken shareable links today.
- The other 109 install a six-method shim, register into it, and then `stem_lab_module.js` (`if (!window.StemLab)`) KEEPS the shim, so the session has no `ensureThree` / `loadScriptResilient` / `setupHiDPI` / viewers. Live probe of `?tool=solarSystem` confirmed: StemLab had exactly the 6 shim keys. Every 3D tool opened from a shared link would report the 3D engine could not load.

Fixed in three layers (this commit):
- ANTI `loadOne` (all three copies): a STEM plugin script is HELD until `AlloModules.StemLab` (or a StemLab with `ensureThree`) exists, bounded at 25 s, and the plugin's own 20 s timeout now starts at injection. Keyed on `window.__alloModuleRegistry`, which the real app creates before the loader and the unit harness lacks, so `stem_plugin_dependency_order.test.js`'s older cases still run the immediate path. Three new cases there cover hold / bound / already-there.
- `stem_lab_module.js` (three copies: `stem_lab/`, `public/stem_lab/`, and the third at `desktop/web-app/public/stem_lab_module.js` that `math_create_modal.test.js` pins): a pre-seeded shim is recognised by its missing `ensureThree`; the full object is built and the shim's registrations re-run through the real `registerTool`. New `tests/stem_lab_module_adopts_plugin_shim.test.js` boots the module under jsdom (it does boot, with React UMD + `AlloModules` + `__alloT`) and checks both orders plus a double run.
- The two new tools use the standard shim instead of a silent return (tests added to both suites).
- Real-host result after the fix, `?tool=` on :3000: scaleExplorer registered, 60 ladder rows, canvas + role=application, 13 StemLab keys, 0 errors; zoomGallery picker + coach; solarSystem registered with `ensureThree` and a live canvas. Request order is now module → plugin.

**Also in this commit, smaller:**
- Catalog: Zoom Gallery and Scale Explorer moved from the tail of "Computing, AI & Digital Literacy" to the tail of "Earth & Space Science" (next to Universe / Galaxy / Solar System); `tool_index` sections follow. Zoom Gallery's `category` is now `'science'` (was v1's `'creative'`, which mapped to the generic STEM subject in the lesson-plan registry); `stem_registry_metadata.test.js` pin updated with the reason.
- `_activeToolFallbackMeta` in the module carried 11 icons as MOJIBAKE TEXT (`'ðŸ§ª'` etc., a Latin-1 round trip at some point), plus the default. ## 2026-09-13 — Scale Explorer / Zoom Gallery: links that name a place

The 09-13 deploy carried 93d3a517a: `tests/e2e/85-deep-link-registers-plugin.spec.ts` is 5/5 against the live CDN, so `/scale-explorer`, `/zoom-gallery` and every other shared link now open their tool. Built on that:

- **`?tool=scaleExplorer&focus=<itemId>`** opens Scale Explorer at that item (e.g. `focus=rbc`, `focus=oort`); **`&at=<power of ten>`** opens at that exponent with the nearest item in focus (`at=-9` → the DNA helix). State AND the animation refs are initialised from the link, so there is no fly-in from the person.
- **`?tool=zoomGallery&image=<id>`** opens straight onto an image (`image=bootprint`, `image=pillars`); `custom` is refused.
- Both read their parameter ONLY when `?tool=` names them (normalised like the host: lowercase, non-alphanumerics stripped), so one tool's `focus=` cannot steer another. Verified live that the host keeps `location.search` after boot.
- **"Copy link to this view" / "Copy link to this image"** buttons (In Focus card; Zoom Gallery header row when an image is open). Copy goes through `window.alloCopyText` (Canvas-safe) → async clipboard → textarea fallback; on failure the link is shown in a read-only field for hand copying, and SR gets "Link to {name} copied." The link points at the current origin on an AlloFlow host and at `https://alloflow-cdn.pages.dev/app/` from anywhere a class cannot reach (Canvas `usercontent.goog`, localhost, the desktop app).
- Strings: 7 new `stem.scaleExplorer.*`, 6 new `stem.zoomGallery.*` (INL, not WIN, so the pop-out's STR parity holds) in all four ui_strings copies via the section-owning scripts. English only, like the rest of both sections.
- Tests: scale_explorer +4, zoom_gallery_catalog +3 (lifted module functions against a fake window: gating, validation, nearest-item, share base), spec 85 +2 (post-deploy). Real host on :3000 (`react-scripts start` now needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, it OOMs at the 4 GB default): `focus=rbc` landed on the red blood cell, `image=bootprint` opened the bootprint with OSD tiles, clipboard held the public links, `at=999` and `focus=nonsense` fell back to the person.

## 2026-09-13 — Scale Explorer: showing an order of magnitude instead of naming it

Aaron asked for approaches that keep the tool "engaging, rich and visually illustrative, particularly showing different orders of magnitude". Built three now, verified in the real host on :3000:
- **Nested decade frames on the stage.** Inside the focused object: a dashed square a tenth as wide (÷10) and a hundredth (÷100, when ≥ 6 px), backed so they read over the emoji, plus a dashed guide from the ÷10 square down to the axis point one decade LEFT of the focus. That line is the whole lesson: a tenth of the width is one step left. The ×10 frame is off the stage by construction (the focus fills ~42% of the shorter side), which is why the frames nest inward.
- **The ×10 staircase under Compare.** The ratio as a chain of whole decades, each chip a real object at that decade (person → ×10 T. rex → ×10 pyramid → ×10 [1.7 km, bare] → ×10 Everest → ×10 Chicxulub → ×10 reef → ×7.5 Earth). Examples are the nearest ladder item within half a decade, never an endpoint; the remainder is the last arrow. Universe→proton is 41 steps (43 chips) and wraps cleanly. `ol` with an aria-label; arrows are aria-hidden.
- **Scientific notation toggle** ("Also show sizes in scientific notation"): `lengthText()` is the single writer for the focus card, ladder, selects and staircase; the stage labels switch too. Persisted in the tool slice (`sci`).
- Stage now has `maxHeight: max(420px, 78vh)`: the aside can be long (the staircase) and the stage was stretching with it.

Ideas not built, in order I would do them: (4) a continuous "play the zoom" film mode from the person to the universe and down to the proton with the existing per-decade narration (stepwise journey exists; needs a reduced-motion fallback); (5) side-by-side tiling for two things within ~2 decades ("four basketballs across a door"), handing off to the staircase beyond; (6) a decade-population strip under the stage, "your height" personalisation of the person, and a soft pitch per decade for low-vision students.

ui_strings: committed from a HEAD+section blob again (another session's 195 sourcebook keys are still in the working tree); this time in HEAD's key order, so the hunk is the three new keys only.

**Same day, film mode (this commit):** "▶ Play the zoom out to the universe" / "▶ Play the zoom in to the proton" with a Slow/Normal/Fast speed (0.35 / 0.7 / 1.4 powers of ten per second, persisted). One unbroken constant-rate zoom on its own rAF, frame-time based; the focus card, stage labels and per-decade SR line keep up on their own; a progress strip and a "10ⁿ m · length" caption are painted on the stage while it plays. Space on the stage plays/pauses (shift+space inward); any manual navigation (buttons, wheel, scrubber, ladder, End) stops it; it ends 0.4 decades past the ladder's last item with the existing "as far as the ladder goes" line. Reduced motion falls back to the stepwise journey and the panel says so. Measured on :3000: ~1.4 dec/s at fast, pause/resume via space, manual stop, ends at 27.30 on the observable universe. Also fixed "1 times the Earth–Sun distance" on the AU rung.

**Same day, tiling + population strip (this commit):** Compare now shows side-by-side tiling for two things within two powers of ten (the small one repeated across the width of the big one: emoji copies when a copy is ≥ 14 px, alternating cells otherwise, a dimmer part-cell for the remainder; the sentence is the SVG's accessible name; under 1.5× it says "nearly the same size"). It hands off to the ×10 staircase above two decades; between one and two both show. The scrubber now carries a population strip on its own axis: one column per power of ten, height = number of ladder items at that size; 6 of the 44 decades are empty and that shows. Decorative to readers (aria-hidden; the ladder lists everything); click a column to go there. Verified on :3000.

**Not built, with a reason:** "your height" personalisation of the person. `ITEMS` is a module-level constant that `sorted`, `byId`, the link reader, the staircase and the stage all close over; making one item's size per-instance means threading a derived list through all of them. Worth doing, but as its own pass with the harness ready, not tacked onto this one.

**Same day, theme audit + "your height" (this commit):** axe over the new UI (tiling, staircase, notation, film controls) in dark / light / contrast: 0 violations, 0 incomplete; staircase endpoint chips 8.2:1 to 12.6:1; contrast-theme film frame eyeballed (caption, progress strip, frames legible). Then the deferred personalisation: "Make the person your height: [cm] Use my height", shown when the person is in focus and always once set; 50–250 cm; the person becomes "You" (card) / "you" (sentences) at that size, persisted in the slice (`yourHeightCm`), re-centres on set/clear, "Back to average" restores 1.7 m. Implementation: `items` = ITEMS with the human swapped, `sorted`/`byId` derive from it, and the stage + `nearestItem` read the list through `sortedRef` (the rAF closure outlives the render; without the ref the last frame after a change painted the old person at the new camera). Verified on :3000 including persistence across close/reopen.

Four images now carry a reference length and show a map-style scale bar that follows the zoom, plus "This view is {w} across" and "⚖️ See this size in Scale Explorer" (sets `window.__alloScaleExplorerStart = {exp}` and switches tools; Scale Explorer reads it at mount and clears it in its mount effect, not in the initialiser, because StrictMode double-runs initialisers and the first probe consumed it).

## 2026-09-13 — ★★★ Live defect: the service worker broke every returning visitor's first reload

Found while verifying the 15:46 deploy: with the worker active, ANY second navigation in the same tab (a plain reload of /app/ included) failed with net::ERR_FAILED; with service workers blocked it worked. Chain, each link measured on the live app: Pages answers `/app/index.html` with a 308 to `/app/` → the install step's `cache.addAll(['./index.html', …])` stored a response with `redirected: true` → a navigation request may not be served a redirected response (its redirect mode is not "follow") → Chrome fails the load → the navigate handler's background refetch replaced the entry with a clean copy, so the NEXT reload worked. So: one dead reload per install or update, for everyone, since the precache list gained `./index.html`. Fresh-context tests never navigate twice, which is why no spec saw it.

Fix (template `desktop/web-app/public/sw.js` + stamped `app/sw.js` + its mirror, identical; the two `build.js` string-replace anchors untouched): a `cleanCopy()` that re-wraps a redirected response before it is cached; install fetches each precache path and `put`s the clean copy (still all-or-nothing); the navigate handler never serves a stored entry with `redirected: true` and cleans what it writes back. New `tests/service_worker_redirected_shell.test.js` serves the real worker behind a local server that 308s exactly like Pages and drives Chromium: install, then reload. Proven against both: the HEAD worker fails (`ERR_FAILED`), the fixed one passes. Ships with the next deploy; once the new worker activates, its cache is clean, so no further failed reloads.

Also noted while here: `tests/qr_student_shell` "keeps the QR/privacy sections synchronized across all three app copies" is red on the working tree because all three ANTI copies carry another session's in-flight edits; not touched.

**18:58 — deploy attempt for the worker fix STOPPED by deploy.sh itself (Step 0.8, exit 1), and I left it stopped.** `vitest --changed` runs the tests related to everything dirty against HEAD; the working tree carries another session's in-flight ANTI rewrite of the live-session/mailbox area (+692/−254 lines, last write 17:07), and `tests/class_mailbox.test.js` is red: 3 of its pins fail on the working tree and they fail against HEAD's ANTI too (they expect text like `a: 'putsubmission'` that the extraction wave moved out of ANTI), so they are stale pins, not a regression of the moment. Two things must happen before the next deploy: (1) the mailbox session lands or reverts its ANTI edit; (2) its owner updates the `class_mailbox` pins for the post-extraction layout. `SKIP_CHANGED_TESTS=1 ./deploy.sh` exists as a bypass; I recommend against it here, because the same run would publish the half-finished ANTI. The worker fix (3c7828121) and the new boot-spec check (`01-app-boot`: reload twice with the worker active, currently RED against the live CDN by design, GREEN once the fixed worker is deployed) are committed and waiting.

**Same evening, four rungs + reduced-motion check (this commit):** Scale Explorer's ladder had six empty decades; four now carry something well defined: one light minute (1.799e10 m, 10¹⁰), one light month (7.77e14 m, 10¹⁵), the distance to the Coma Cluster (3.0e24 m, 10²⁴, with an uncertainty note; Zwicky 1933), ten billion light years (9.461e25 m, 10²⁶). 10⁻¹⁶ and 10⁻¹³ stay empty on purpose (nothing has a defined width below the proton; nothing familiar at 100 fm) and the test now pins exactly those two. 64 items; the film crosses fewer blank stretches; the strip shows 42/44 filled. Verified in the real host under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: the note shows, Play falls back to the stepwise journey (whole decades every 2.4 s, pause control present).

**Same evening, pop-out parity (this commit):** the companion window (`zoom_gallery/zoom_gallery.html`) now draws the same scale bar as the inline tool for the five scale images (same `scale` data, same mapping via `imageToViewerElementCoordinates`, same round-length picker; hidden on the picker, on return, and on images without a scale). The three shared strings (`scale_group`, `scale_about`, `scale_view`) moved from the tool's INL to WIN so the pop-out's STR can carry them under the pinned WIN==STR parity. Measure and the challenge stay inline-only. Verified in a real browser served from the working tree: Earthrise 20,000 km at home, 5000 km after two zooms, bar hidden on Bootprint.
